# Refresh records, format 1: WEB-BUILT EJECTS vectors
# r3, r5 and r7 were made by the web's builder, the rest by hand:
#  r1 genesis by A; r2 by A: B, C (admin), D, E, F in (X_invitation by A at v1);
#  r3 A's EJECT of D, counted: D removed;
#  r4 by admin C: E and F carried PENDING only, newcomer N in (N_invitation by C at v3);
#  r5 A's REPAIR on a browser where r4 is rejected (N unconfirmed; F off its list; E listed with new keys
#     E_new_*, unconfirmed): E pending, F filled departed, N pending, link 5->4;
#  r6 by admin C: N included again, newcomer M in (M_invitation by C at v5);
#  r7 A's EJECT of M on a browser where r6 is rejected (M, N unconfirmed): M, not counted there but named by r6,
#     passed off the list and named REMOVED, link 7->6.
# S = derive_key(circle_secret, key_v1); issued_at of every built record = now. Importers the web checks (and the SDK
# should): B's device step by step, holding key_vN at step N, listing (confirmed unless said): steps 1-2 A (owner),
# B, C (admin), D, E, F with their invitations; 3: A, B, C, E, F; 4: + N (N_invitation); 5: A, B, C, E with E_new
# keys (unconfirmed), N; 6: + M (M_invitation); 7: A, B, C, E (E_new, unconfirmed), N -> every version accepted;
# then D, F, M not counted, N and E members. A's device, the same with N and M unconfirmed (listed as the header of
# r5/r7 says, M off the list at step 7) -> r4 and r6 rejected (R2 unmatched entry), every other version accepted,
# sealing v7.
